sentences.text: Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appell  Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER

The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 12.04.2024 passed by the XVIII Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.3131/2021 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The issue regarding the accident and the liability of the Insurance Company is not in dispute.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 24/01/2021 at around 11:00 pm the appellant was returning after closing his shop for the day situated at Sai Kripa Colony, Indore through his motorcycle.

When he reached near Toll Naka at A.B. Road, Indore a Maruti Car bearing registration number MP-09- CE-4617, which was being driven by its Driver in rash and negligent manner dashed into the motorcycle of the appellant, because of which the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21012 2 MA-6452-2024 suffered grievous injuries on his waste and right leg.
3.1 The appellant / claimant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.
The Claims Tribunal after assessing the evidence on record, concluded that there was no permanent disability.

The total compensation of Rs.2,25,576/- was awarded for sustaining injuries, towards medical expenses, etc.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant / claimant submits that the Claims Tribunal has erred in not accepting the claim of the appellant for permanent disability.

He by referring the statement of Dr.
Sruendra Bapat (AW-2) submits that there is 30% reduction in the movement capacity because of fracture in Acetabulum Bone of the left hip and because of the fracture in Tibia and Calcaneus Bone of right leg, Rod was inserted, because of which there is swelling and pain.

There is reduction of 20%
in the movement of knee and reduction of 20% in the movement of ankle.

He also refers to Ex.-
Roshan vs Jagdish Dangi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80983032/
1 P/38, which is a Permanent Disability Certificate issued by the said Doctor and submits that there was no reason to disbelieve the Permanent Disability Certificate by the Claims Tribunal.

He thus,
stresses that the permanent disability of the appellant should be taken as 20% and for the injuries sustained, the amount in all other heads including special diet, attendant, transportation, pain and suffering and loss of income should be enhanced.

5 . Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company by referring to findings of the Claims Tribunal in para 16 to 18 of the impugned award submits that the evidence regarding permanent disability NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21012 3 MA-6452-2024 was not at all trustworthy.

He also submits that the Claims Tribunal has awarded adequate compensation including compensation for loss of income for a period of two months, thus, no inference is warranted with the award passed by the Claims Tribunal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
7.

The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant regarding permanent disability in terms of Ex.-P/38, if examined in light of deposition of appellant (AW-1) himself as well as Dr. Surendra Bapat (AW-2) it is seen that in para 11 of his cross-examination the appellant accepted that fractures sustained by him have fully united.

He also admits in the same para that he has taken the Permanent Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/38) by paying fees to Dr. Bapat as also the fact that the said certificate has not been issued by his treating doctor.

Apart from this, Dr. Surendra Bapat (AW-2)
admits in para 11 of his cross-examination that he has not issued certificate in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Government of India in the year 2018.
He also admits in para 13 of his cross-examination that the fractures of the appellants are united.
He stated on his own that there was deposition of callus on the joint.
He has further admitted in the same para that in the Report of X-ray (Ex.-P/40) the word 'Callus' was added in handwriting, which was originally not there.
It has also been admitted in para 6 of his cross-examination by the said doctor that he is not the treating doctor of the appellant.

8. In view of all above facts, the evidence with regard to permanent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21012 4 MA-6452-2024 disability is not at all trustworthy.
It does not inspire confidence at all.
In the considered view of this Court, no interference is warranted in the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in respect of the permanent disability.
9. As regards the injuries sustained by the appellant, it is indisputable that he sustained fractures in his right Tibia and Calcaneus Bone and also left hip / Acetabulum Bone.
Apart from this, he suffered injuries on other parts of his body.
It is thus, seen that though the appellant has not sustained any permanent disability, but he certainly suffered grievous injuries at more than one place of his body.
10. Looking to this fact, the amount of compensation of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering is very less.
Thus, in the considered view of this Court a lump sum amount of Rs.1,50,000/- would be adequate for sustaining such grievous injuries.
As such, the appellant be paid a further amount of Rs.1,50,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

This amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before Roshan vs Jagdish Dangi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80983032/
2 the Claims Tribunal.
11. In the above terms, the present appeal stands disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Roshan vs Jagdish Dangi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80983032/
